option_relations.rationale: Statin-induced rhabdomyolysis leading to acute tubular necrosis is a specific cause of rhabdomyolysis-induced acute kidney injury, which is the provided leaf diagnosis. The vignette supports statin as a potential cause.
Relugolix is not mentioned in the vignette as a medication the patient was taking, nor is there any information to suggest it as a cause of rhabdomyolysis in this case.
Rhabdomyolysis-induced acute kidney injury is the exact diagnosis provided in the leaf. The vignette describes findings consistent with this condition.

Prolonged immobility can cause rhabdomyolysis, which in turn can lead to acute kidney injury. The patient had a fall and was briefly immobilized, making this a potential contributing factor to the rhabdomyolysis, which then led to the acute kidney injury. Thus, it is a supertype of the leaf diagnosis.
